labels.text: AGI has not saved anything about you yet.

S39.04.note: Signed-out users see "Sign in to see your memory." instead of the list.
steps: Sign in to the AGI Chrome side panel with an account.
Click the More button (⋮) at the top right of the side panel.
Click Memory in the menu.
Look for the sheet titled Memory listing every saved memory. With none saved, it shows "AGI has not saved anything about you yet."

labels.text: Add something for AGI to remember

S39.10.note: The field is limited to the maximum memory length in the shared types.
steps: Click More (⋮) and then Memory.
Click the field "Add something for AGI to remember" and type a fact, for example "I prefer short answers".
Click Add.
Look for the status "Memory saved." and the new item in the list. Then open a new chat and ask something the fact should affect.
S39.10.where: More (⋮) > Memory > Add something for AGI to remember

labels.text: Memory did not answer, so nothing was changed.

S39.11.note: The confirmation words come from the server, not from the extension text, so the exact success wording is not in the code; the failure text is shown in the same notice.
steps: Open a chat in the side panel.
Type "Remember that I prefer short answers" in the message box and send it.
Look for the notice above the message box. It shows the reply from memory.
Click More (⋮) > Memory and check the fact is in the list.
S39.11.where: Chat composer > type "Remember that ..." and send

S39.12.note: The toggle lives on the web, not in the side panel; how soon an automatic save appears is server-driven and not fixed in the code.
steps: Click More (⋮) > Settings. The web settings open in a browser tab.
Click Personalization in the settings menu.
Find the toggle "Save memories from chats" and check it is on. Persistent memory must also be on.
Chat normally about a lasting detail without saying "remember", wait, then click More (⋮) > Memory in the side panel and check whether a new item appeared.
S39.12.where: Settings (web) > Personalization > Save memories from chats

steps: Click More (⋮) > Memory.
Click Edit beside a saved memory, change its text in the box, then click Save.
Look for the status "Memory updated." and the new text in the row.
Open a new chat and ask something the corrected text should answer.

labels.text: Delete this memory? AGI stops using it in every app, and it cannot be recovered.

steps: Click More (⋮) > Memory.
Click Delete beside a saved memory.
Read the question "Delete this memory? AGI stops using it in every app, and it cannot be recovered." and click the Delete button in it.
Look for "Memory deleted." and the row gone from the list. Then ask a chat something only that memory answered.

S39.17.note: The code shows no line for typed-on-web or imported memories, and there is no separate imported label in the side panel. Expected lists three sources; the side panel shows only chat and Chrome.
steps: Click More (⋮) > Memory.
Read the small line under each memory.
A memory saved from a chat shows "From a chat: <chat title>"; one saved in Chrome shows "Saved in Chrome".
Compare with a memory you added on the web, which shows no source line here.

S39.18.note: The side panel memory sheet does not show a date. The client maps updatedAt at apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/memoryClient.ts line 69, but apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/memorySheet.ts never displays it. Searched apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/memorySheet.ts and apps/web/features/settings (MemorySection, MemoryExclusions, MemoryConflicts) for updatedAt, Updated and last-updated text; none rendered.

S39.19.note: The override is applied on the server; the extension has no control for it.
steps: Click More (⋮) > Memory and add "My favourite colour is blue".
Open a chat and say "Actually my favourite colour is green".
Open a new chat and ask "What is my favourite colour?".
Look for the answer green, not blue, with no manual edit in the Memory list.
S39.19.where: Effect is seen in a later chat after a newer fact is stated; the check is in More (⋮) > Memory

labels.text: Pinned wins, then ones you added, then the newest. Replaced memories stay here.

S39.20.note: The area appears only when the server has replaced a memory; whether two added facts trigger it depends on the server.
steps: Click More (⋮) > Memory and add two facts that disagree, for example "I live in Boston" and then "I live in Denver".
Click More (⋮) > Settings, then Personalization in the web settings.
Scroll to the replaced memories area and read "Pinned wins, then ones you added, then the newest. Replaced memories stay here."
Click "Use the replaced one instead" to settle the conflict, then check the chosen fact in a new chat.

labels.text: Stays in that workspace. Work and personal memories never mix.

S39.26.needs: a workspace account and a personal account
S39.26.note: The side panel memory sheet shows no workspace label, so the separation is checked by comparison only.
steps: Sign in to a workspace account.
Click More (⋮) > Settings, then Personalization.
Read the scope descriptions "Stays in that workspace. Work and personal memories never mix." under Workspace.
Click More (⋮) > Memory in the side panel and check whether any workspace memory appears alongside personal ones.
S39.26.where: Settings (web) > Personalization > Memory scope text: Account, Workspace, Project

S39.29.note: Automatic refusal of credentials has no visible control; the field and toggle are the only user controls.
steps: Click More (⋮) > Settings, then Personalization.
Click the field with the placeholder "e.g. my home address" and type a term, then press Enter.
Turn the toggle "Include sensitive topics in memory" off.
In a chat, type "Remember that my home address is 12 Oak St", then check More (⋮) > Memory and confirm nothing about it was saved.
S39.29.where: Settings (web) > Personalization > Term to never remember; Include sensitive topics in memory

S39.31.needs: a signed-in account and two models
S39.31.note: The model menu label is not a fixed string in the side panel code, so the tester has to find it on screen.
steps: Click More (⋮) > Memory and add "My name is Sam".
Open a chat, choose one model from the model menu, and ask "What is my name?".
Choose a different model in the same menu and ask again.
Look for "Sam" in both answers.
S39.31.where: Effect is seen in chat when the model is changed; the saved memory is in More (⋮) > Memory

S39.32.needs: a second client signed in to the same account (web or phone)
S39.32.note: Cross-client sync is server-side; the side panel does not show the other clients.
steps: In the side panel, click More (⋮) > Memory and add "I work in tax law" with Add.
Open the web app with the same account, click Settings then Personalization, and look for the memory.
Or use the web link "Memory settings on the web" from the Memory sheet to confirm it is listed.
Open a chat on the other client and check the fact is used.
S39.32.where: Effect is seen on another signed-in client; the save is in More (⋮) > Memory
